<findings>
<finding task="0"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>R1.3: `compatibility` is "a string of 1–500 UTF-8 bytes after stripping".</plan><fix>Under "Values copied verbatim from the spec", quote R1.3 as written: "a string of 1–500 characters after stripping". In Task 3, measure `len(compat.strip())`, change the error message and test to "1-500 characters", and drop the UTF-8-bytes rationale line. To keep a byte cap instead, add a spec amendment to Task 1 and get the owner to approve it, rather than presenting the changed wording as a verbatim quote.</fix></finding>
<finding task="1"><quote>R1.9 The module docstring describes the new rules and the `--strict` flag, and CLAUDE.md's Commands section gains the `--strict` invocation with one line on when to use it</quote><plan>- **D7** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-18): Task 7 names `--strict` in the frontmatter lint's existing CLAUDE.md comment and adds no line. Applied in: Task 7.</plan><fix>D7 changes what R1.9 requires: no invocation line is added, only a comment clause. That makes it a spec-level decision. Add an amendment A12 to Task 1 with an exact replace-this-with-that block for R1.9, tagged `(owner, plan 53, 2026-10-18)`. Change D7's "Applied in" to "Task 1 (spec amendment A12), Task 7", and raise Task 1 Step 2's expected `grep -c` to 12.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>Without uv, run the same path with `python3` in an environment that has the dependencies listed in the script's header.</quote><plan>## Decisions</plan><fix>The plan has no `## Review Focus` section, which the plan header requires. Add one between Global Constraints and Decisions, listing the five uncovered failure modes most likely to bite a user, each with a pinning test in the task where it would fail. Candidates: the `python3` fallback with no uv actually runs a stdlib-only script (Task 11); a script whose existing shebang is not `#!/usr/bin/env python3` still ends up with that shebang on line 1 after `add_headers.py` (R3.2; Task 10); stale header-less llm-wiki installed copies run inside a Python project (DF15; Task 11); a non-ASCII `compatibility` value at the cap (Task 3); and a `LICENSE*` copy that `install.py --copy --skill` fails to carry (Task 8).</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>**State test changes as +N deltas** against the suite, never absolute totals.</quote><plan>Each expected summary line below is what the replay printed on top of `d70e0b3`; on a later base the absolute counts may differ, the deltas may not.</plan><fix>Restate every expected pytest summary as a delta against the run just before the step. For example, Task 3 Step 2 becomes "+4 tests, all 4 new ones failed, no other failure", and Step 6 becomes "+4 passed, no failure". Drop absolute totals such as `45 passed`, `4 failed, 41 passed` and `64 passed` throughout Tasks 3–12 and the per-suite counts in Task 10 Step 6, so the plan meets the spec's constraint instead of explaining why it departs from it.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>Next step: an implementation plan from the writing-plans skill.</quote><plan>**Edit `build/check_frontmatter.py`: insert before the line `def check_skill(skill_dir: Path) -> list[str]:`:**</plan><fix>The plan is far more than five times the spec's length. It is a transcript: complete function bodies (`_check_value_shapes`, `_check_invocation_parity`, `bundled_license_violations`, `required_imports`, `check_script_headers`, `bundled_invocations`, …) that the signatures plus the pinned test assertions already determine, and a Planning record that restates facts. Replace those bodies with signatures, the spec values they pin and their tests. Keep code only for algorithms the tests leave open (the PEP 723 regex, the `RUNNER_RE` and continuation handling, the Stage D kit's exact prompt copy). Condense the Planning record to the decisions and measurements the implementer needs.</fix></finding>
</findings>
